props.gloss_en: an etrog of orla is unfit
one said: [an orla etrog is unfit] because it has no permission to be eaten
and one said: [an orla etrog is unfit] because it has no monetary standing
(entertained) whoever requires permission to eat does not require monetary standing, and whoever requires monetary standing does not require permission to eat
the mishnah: an etrog of impure teruma is unfit (cited by תנן at 35a.8)
impure teruma has monetary standing: [the priest] burns it as fuel under his cooking
on permission to eat, all agree that it is required
one holds: permission to eat is required, monetary standing is not
and one holds: monetary standing is required too
second tithe in Jerusalem has permission to be eaten
according to R' Meir, second tithe is the property of the Most High

per the Sages: with it a person fulfils his obligation on the festival
per R' Meir: with matza of second tithe a person does not fulfil his obligation on Pesach
per the Sages: with it a person fulfils his obligation on Pesach
per R' Meir: dough of second tithe is exempt from challa
per the Sages: it is liable to challa
Rav Pappa: granted dough -- 'the first of YOUR dough' is written
Rav Pappa: the etrog too -- 'for yourselves' is written: from your own

schemas.gloss_en: כתיב הכא לחם עוני, וכתיב התם והיה באכלכם מלחם הארץ: מה להלן משלכם ולא משל מעשר, אף כאן משלכם ולא משל מעשר (35a.13-35b.1; ואיתימא Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya)

supports.gloss_en: R' Asi said: per R' Meir one does not fulfil with a second-tithe etrog, per the Sages one does -- the shape of the monetary-standing dispute, so he is its author (תסתיים)

לימא מסייע ליה: dough of second tithe is exempt from challa, R' Meir; the Sages: liable. [היא היא -- it is the dough clause itself;] אלא: מדבהא פליגי, בהא נמי פליגי -- since they dispute dough, they dispute matza too

deflected_by.gloss_en: או דלמא שאני עיסה, דאמר קרא עריסותיכם עריסותיכם תרי זימני -- or perhaps dough is different, for the verse says 'your dough' twice

objections.gloss_en: תנן: של תרומה טמאה פסולה -- fine for the permission-to-eat view; but for the monetary-standing view, why? he burns it under his cooking (= p_masika_tachat_tavshilo)

answered_by.gloss_en: אתיא לחם לחם: 'bread of affliction' here, 'the bread of the land' there; as there from yours and not from tithe, so here (= gs_lechem_lechem, p_matza_mishelachem)
